note: Prototype cases, written to be reviewed. kind: positive = must load the expected skills; negative = must not load the forbidden ones; confusable = a neighbouring skill looks applicable but is not. Skills not listed in expect, forbid or allow are reported as extras. given-when-then-format and requirements-elicitation are allowed everywhere: any requirements task writes acceptance criteria and may need elicitation.

cases.prompt: Here is a one-line ticket from the backlog: "Improve search". Write the requirements.

Azure DevOps work item 1423: "As a customer I want to reset my password". Write the requirements for the sprint team.
Jira story PAY-88 goes into the next Scrum sprint. Split it if needed and write its acceptance criteria.

Add an export-to-CSV button to the internal reports page of our existing ERP. Write the requirements.
Write the requirements for a new feature in our internal HR portal: employees request leave.
Review these acceptance criteria and rewrite them so they are testable: "The system should be fast and user friendly".
Write the acceptance criteria for a login form that locks the account after five failed attempts.
A client emailed us a complete, detailed specification for two-factor authentication. Turn it into requirements; there is no backlog or sprint involved.
El cliente dice que quiere "algo para controlar mejor los pedidos". Redacta los requisitos.
